chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn, from al-Qāsim, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub while he has with him only enough water to suffice for his wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer): should he perform wudu (ablution) with the water, or perform tayammum? He said: “He performs tayammum. Do you not see that half of purification has been appointed for him?”

key_terms.لِلصَّلَاةِ: for salat (prayer), the act of worship requiring taharah
key_terms.لِوُضُوئِهِ: for his wudu (ablution), the lesser ritual purification
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: enters the state of janabah, requiring ritual purification

ai.seo_question: If a junub person has only enough water for wudu (ablution), should he use it or perform tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who is in a state of janabah and possesses only a small amount of water insufficient for ghusl. The Imam عليه السلام rules that he should perform tayammum, indicating that in such a case tayammum serves as the legislated substitute purification.
